headline: High: shared-file and clipboard bridges make prompt injection, leakage, and output-cascade plausible; ChatGPT Desktop’s default file/screen ingestion raises the pair’s risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and touches CLAUDE.md/project notes, while ChatGPT Desktop can ingest clipboard, files, screenshots, and app context. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from caveman can be copied or surfaced into ChatGPT and treated as instructions. The pathway is not proven by direct pair evidence, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF caveman output is copied into ChatGPT Desktop via clipboard or file import, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is granted access to app context or screenshots containing caveman text, instruction hijacking risk increases.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents.
Keep caveman outputs in a separate review-only file.
Strip instructions from any text pasted into ChatGPT Desktop.
Use a human checklist before acting on copied content.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and files from supported macOS apps, and also captures screenshots. If the same workspace or app context is exposed to both, sensitive project data can flow into OpenAI-hosted processing. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium fits the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF caveman stores sensitive notes in files that ChatGPT Desktop can read from supported macOS apps, leakage occurs.
IF screenshots or uploads include session logs or memory files, those contents can leave the local workspace.
mitigations: Move sensitive notes out of shared folders.
Turn off Work-with-Apps for sensitive sessions.
Avoid uploading caveman-generated files to ChatGPT Desktop.
Review screenshots before sending them.
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances, but ChatGPT Desktop has write_filesystem=false and modify_git_state=false, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The main overlap is read-side interaction through files and app context, not concurrent mutation of the same state. Because caveman’s filesystem write capability is not explicitly listed, uncertainty stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF caveman is configured to write into a shared directory that ChatGPT Desktop also reads, read/write contention can appear.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents mutable access to the same git repo, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Keep ChatGPT Desktop out of the repo working tree.
Use separate folders for each agent.
Avoid simultaneous edits to the same files.
Check git status before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md-style content, and ChatGPT Desktop can consume files, screenshots, and connected-app context. That makes it plausible for ChatGPT to treat caveman output as authoritative and then rewrite or act on it without verification. No direct evidence shows automatic action-taking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF caveman-generated notes are fed into ChatGPT Desktop without a verification step, errors can cascade.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to summarize or transform caveman output for downstream use, mistaken facts can propagate.
mitigations: Require a second human review of any transformed output.
Compare ChatGPT summaries against the original caveman file.
Mark caveman output as untrusted input.
Use a template that forces citation of source lines.
requires-engineering: add automated diff-and-verify checks.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while ChatGPT Desktop processes uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code under vendor-hosted services. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for retention and residency if regulated data is placed into both systems. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman files and then uploaded to ChatGPT Desktop, retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF the operator relies on ChatGPT Desktop for data subject deletion or export, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Use separate retention policies for each workspace.
Document which data classes may be uploaded.
Review vendor terms before processing sensitive files.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
